Full story: This visualization compares advertising revenue (in billions USD) for four platform giants from 2007 through 2026. Values through 2024 are based on company annual reports and market-research tallies (Alphabet investor relations; Meta investor relations; Amazon investor relations; Statista; eMarketer/Insider Intelligence; public Analyst reports). 2025–2026 are marked as estimates where noted in the timeline labels.

Why this matters: TikTok (ByteDance) went from near-zero ad revenue to a multi‑billion-dollar ad competitor inside a few years — creating a dramatic reallocation of ad spend from search and feed into short-form video. Watch the race: one platform soars (TikTok), one stays dominant but faces share erosion (Google), one plateaus then regains (Meta), and one grows steadily off retail intent (Amazon Ads).

instagram_caption:
🚨 Attention Heist: $0 → $42B in 10 years — the ad market’s biggest robbery

In 2007 Google pulled in about $16.9B in ad revenue and dominated the internet. Fast-forward to 2021 and Google still sits atop a $200B+ ad pile, but the map of attention has already started to change.

Meta (Facebook) went from $0.15B in 2007 to a peak of roughly $114.9B by 2021 — a meteoric climb that rewired the newsfeed economy. Amazon quietly built a retail-intent ad behemoth, rising from near-zero in the late 2000s to roughly $37.7B by 2022.

Then came TikTok. From effectively zero before 2017 to $11.6B in 2022 — and our timeline projects a leap to about $42.0B by 2026 (2025–2026 are marked estimates). That’s the plot twist: a platform that didn’t exist globally in 2016 is now stealing ad dollars from search, social feeds and video, forcing incumbent giants to fight back with short-form products and new ad formats.

This dataset shows the narrative in cold numbers: Google stays huge ($16.9B → $260B est. 2026), Meta climbs then flattens ($0.15B → $150B est. 2026), Amazon grows steadily ($0 → $72B est. 2026), and TikTok explodes ($0 → $42B est. 2026). Watch how the lines cross — those crossing points are boardroom-level crisis moments and advertiser pivot points.

What do you think will happen next — will TikTok keep eating share, or will incumbents claw some back? Drop your prediction and the year you think TikTok hits $100B (if it does!).

Attention Heist — How TikTok is re-routing ad dollars (2007–2026)

This timeline compares advertising revenue (in billions USD) for Google (Alphabet), Meta (Facebook), Amazon Advertising, and TikTok (ByteDance) from 2007 through projected 2026. Key milestones: Google grows from $16.9B (2007) to an estimated $260B (2026 est.); Meta moves from $0.15B (2007) to roughly $150B (2026 est.); Amazon Advertising scales from near-zero to an estimated $72B (2026 est.); TikTok erupts from zero to $11.6B (2022) and is projected to reach $42B by 2026 (est.).

The data shows a clear story: incumbents remain massive, but share is being siphoned off by new formats — short-form video and discovery-driven shopping represent the most disruptive shifts. Figures through 2024 are based on company reports and industry research; 2025–2026 are identified as estimates in the timeline.

Sources: Alphabet annual reports; Meta investor filings; Amazon investor relations; eMarketer / Insider Intelligence / Statista estimates; industry reporting on ByteDance/TikTok ad revenues.
